# Add S3 datastore-based usage measurement

Measurement configurations need a `"datastoreBased"` mode for S3 ingestion. Its `measurementConfiguration` contains `platform: "s3"` and the customer's string `accountId`; returned and persisted configuration also includes the generated `iamRoleArn`, `externalId`, `ingestion`, `dlq`, and `region` fields. Omitted platform and region default to `"s3"` and `"us-east-1"`. Creating a measurement must provision a uniquely named IAM role and policy scoped to that business's ingestion and DLQ prefixes, trusting the customer account with a fresh external ID. Updating the account must update role trust while preserving that role and external ID.

The internal S3 connector posts `{ message, s3Key }`, where `message` is one standard usage JSON record and the first `s3Key` segment is the business ID. Valid records must flow through the existing usage service with that business ID. Malformed records must be written to the configured DLQ under the mirrored source key plus `.message.text`, with the failed input and processing metadata; already-relative source keys must work too. Existing API-, agent-, and infrastructure-based measurement behavior must remain unchanged.

Preserve the existing integration boundaries used by this codebase: implement S3 provisioning on `DatastoreAccessInformation.setupAccess`, trust updates on `DatastoreAccessInformation.updateAccess`, orchestration in `MeasurementConfigService.create`, connector delivery on the exported `PrivateAPIUsageController.dbUsage`, and generic DLQ delivery on `StandardMeasurementEntity.publishFailureToDLQ`. Use `DB_MEASUREMENT_BUCKET_NAME`, `DB_MEASUREMENT_DLQ_BUCKET_NAME`, and `AWS_REGION`. The IAM role name is `datastore-<businessID>-<measurementId>`; its trust policy principal is `arn:aws:iam::<accountId>:root` and its external-ID condition must match the returned value. `dbUsage` passes the parsed record to `UsageService.create` with the business ID derived from `s3Key`.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand
I'll explore the codebase to learn existing measurement patterns and where S3 datastore-based usage should plug in.

1: # Paigo Backend
2: 
3: This repository serves to hold the backend infrastructure for Paigo. Specifically it contains the code for the Private and Public API
4: 
5: ### Current Status
6: 
7: Don't break this.
8: [![CI](https://github.com/paigo-tech/paigo-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/paigo-tech/paigo-backend/actions/workflows/main.yml)
9: 
10: # Folder Structure
11: 
12: | .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file  
13: | .eslintrc.cjs - linter configuration only comment out linting rules if there a good reason  
14: | .gitignore - ignored files for source control  
15: | src - source for the api application  
16: | test - automated testing suite running jest, includes unit, integration and E2E tests
17: 
18: # Getting started with Local Development
19: 
20: # Environment
21: 
22: -   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)
23: -   Latest version of NodeJS 14.x `nvm install 14`
24: -   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)
25: -   Latest version of [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/)
26: -   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
27: -   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)
28: -   Latest version of [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) for the local integration test enviornment, see install [here](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation)
29: -   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)
30: 
31: For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.
32: 
33: -   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
34: -   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
35: -   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))
36: -   Helpful for command line navigation [z](https://facilecode.com/how-to-setup-z-jump-around/)
37: 
38: # Setup
39: 
40: 1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.
41: 
42: ```bash
43: aws configure
44: AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
45: AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
46: Default region name [None]: us-east-1
47: Default output format [None]: json
48: ```
49: 
50: 2. Clone the repository.
51: 3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
52: 4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `test-usage-data` bucket, the `test-config` bucket and the `paigo` org. **Case sensitive**.
53: 5. [Get an API Token from the Influx instance](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/security/tokens/create-token/)
54: 6. Create the following file at the root directory of the project named `.env`, where the `INFLUX_URL`, `INFLUX_TOKEN` and `INFLUX_ORG` values are stored
55: 
56: Your token will be different than the one below.
57: 
58: ```txt
59: AUTH0_ISSUER_URL=https://dev-joaofx7i.us.auth0.com/
60: AUTH0_AUDIENCE=https://qnonyh1pc7.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
61: INFLUX_TOKEN=<fill_me_in>
62: INFLUX_ORG=paigo
63: INFLUX_URL=http://localhost:8086
64: STAGE=test
65: STRIPE_TOKEN=<fill_me_in>
66: REDIS_URL=localhost
67: REDIS_PORT=6379
68: ```
69: 
70: 8. Navigate to the project folder you want to work on. Install dependencies. `npm ci`
71: 9. Run `npm run setup:redis`
72: 10. Run tests to ensure all tests passed. `npm run test`
73: 
74: ### Local Integration environment
75: 
76: The local integration environment has a few parts. Locally deployed will be a kind based kubernetes cluster, and then the paigo-backend docker image will be deployed into the kind cluster as a pod. The tests then run against that enviornment. This specifically is testing the `transformer` and `scheduler` functionality.
77: 
78: The `pre-commit` npm script handles setup and teardown of the enviornment, all that is required is the installation of the required dependencies to get the env working.
79: 
80: ### Developing
81: 
82: When working on the project please note the following.
83: 
84: -   Commit directly to main. do not create feature branches and pull requests.
85:     -   Prior to commiting verify that work in good to go with another developer, either through pair programming it with them, or by requesting a sync review of the diff.
86:     -   We are following Trunk based development: https://trunkbaseddevelopment.com/
87: -   Make sure to run linting, building, and testing before committing
88:     -   A dependency, `husky` should setup the pre-commit hook to run which is triggered when you run `git commit -m "MY cool message"` and handles this automagically for you.
89: -   To run the api locally utilize `npm run build && npm run start:generic` with the appropriate values in via the `.env` file.
90: 
91: An example of a local `.env` file is the following
